text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED: autoscaler alert - GPU pool 'inference-prod-1' failing to scale beyond 95% capacity, queue growing (>12k requests)

sre-bot: alert details attached. autoscaler retries hitting max attempts, kube events show Pending pods due to insufficient MIG fragments.

Maya Chen: i'm on it, pulling up queues and recent scale events. can someone grab customer impact?

Diego Rivera: CS says ~18 customers are seeing degraded responses; many requests are queued and timing out with 503s. ticket list: #C-4321, #C-4330.

Liam O'Connor: taking primary on-call. @Maya priority: confirm whether this is pure capacity exhaustion or scheduling fragmentation. quick check: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide` shows many pods Pending with nodeAffinity to nvidia.com/mig-1g.

Elenor Park: logs from scheduler: `ErrImagePull` no, actually `0/30 nodes are available: Insufficient nvidia.com/mig-1g`. but we still have GPUs allocated on machines where free MIG slices are wasted. looks like MIG sizing mismatch.

Maya Chen: confirmed. metric snippet: `inference_gpu_utilization` averaged 60% on some nodes but `available_mig_fragments` is 0 because MIGs are partially used by long-lived low-util pods.

Diego Rivera: quick mitigation thought: can we temporarily cordon lower-util nodes and reschedule to consolidate? we might free contiguous MIG slices. risk: customer jobs might be preempted.

Liam O'Connor: agreed. plan: 1) scale up emergency spare nodes (if cloud quota allows) 2) attempt targeted drain/evict on low-util MIG nodes to consolidate 3) adjust autoscaler max surge to allow faster replacement

ops-runner: running scale-up now: `gcloud compute managed-instance-groups resize inference-gpu-group --size=+6` (kickoff 2098765450)

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Scale-up job started (op-12345). expected add time ~4-6 mins.

Elenor Park: while new nodes join, i'm iterating on a node-selection script to drain pods flagged as best-effort and move them. draft command: ```bash
kubectl get pods -n inference -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.annotations["inference.class"]=="best-effort") | .metadata.name' | xargs -r kubectl evict --force --namespace=inference
```

Maya Chen: careful with force evict; some jobs are stateful. add annotation filter for `ephemeral=true` as well.

Diego Rivera: heads up: autoscaler logs show repeated failures: `scaleUp: no feasible nodes` - scheduler can't pack pods because MIG shapes are mismatched (some nodes are 1g, others 2g) -> binpacking fragmentation.

Liam O'Connor: customer impact update: CS escalated to Enterprise accounts; two paying customers reported timeouts affecting latency SLOs. notify legal/sales in parallel.

incident-bot: :information_source: Handoff reminder: Liam is primary; Maya secondary. Please include `#oncall-handoff` note when leaving.

Maya Chen: executing targeted drains on two low-util 1g nodes now (nodes: gpu-node-12, gpu-node-14). evictions started 2098765600.

ops-runner: new instances reported healthy and joined cluster at 2098765740. autoscaler still slow to place because pods prefer exact MIG label. considering temporary relax: change `nodeSelector` for the queue consumer to accept `mig-2g` fallback.

Elenor Park: i'm drafting a temporary toleration config: `tolerations: - key: "allow-mig-fallback" operator: Exists effect: NoSchedule` then we add label `allow-mig-fallback=true` to a subset to accept larger MIGs. will push as canary.

Diego Rivera: pushing patch to routing: reduce concurrency per container for queued jobs to reduce pressure while we rebalance. quick patch: `MAX_CONCURRENCY=4 -> 2` in deployment env. rolling update started 2098765900.

Liam O'Connor: good. also increased autoscaler max nodes from 120 -> 150 as emergency (will reverse after). note: billing spike incoming.

Maya Chen: drain on gpu-node-12 completed, freed 4 contiguous MIG slices, rescheduler placed 6 pending pods onto those slices at 2098765980. queue drained ~30% in 3m.

ops-runner: scale-up completed, new capacity absorbing additional load. initial customer impact reduced; CS reporting fewer timeouts.

Elenor Park: root cause summary (prelim): mixed MIG sizing across pool + long-lived low-util pods pinned to specific MIG slices => fragmentation and stranded capacity; autoscaler doesn't consider defragmentation cost so it hit scale limits and then queued.

Liam O'Connor: short-term mitigations applied: emergency scale-up, targeted drains, relaxed nodeSelectors, concurrency throttle.

Diego Rivera: next actions: 1) schedule a follow-up to consolidate MIG sizes across the pool (prefer uniform 2g for this workload) 2) add defrag job to periodically detect and consolidate low-util MIGs 3) update autoscaler to consider fragmentation heuristics or prefer packing policies.

Maya Chen: leaving handoff to @Liam in 30m. i'll update postmortem stub and add list of affected customers + timestamps.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident acknowledged. severity: Sev2 -> monitoring thresholds normalizing. closing page at handoff unless new regressions appear.

Liam O'Connor: thanks team. good job moving fast. i'll coordinate postmortem and ops runbook updates. :thumbsup:
